pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1 landed in #39983 three days ago. This PR is the result of profiling the native pipeline on one A800 80GB and one RTX 4090 at 1024x1024 / 40 steps (text-to-image and single reference-image edit) and landing the changes the traces justified. The DiT is GEMM-bound (78% cuBLAS, 16% FA3, no launch gaps above 1%), so the lossless DiT work is a small win; the VAE had clear layout and fusion waste; and two harness gaps made `--attention-backend sage_attn` edits and the opt-in HTTP tests fail as documented.

Every commit is independent and reviewable on its own; happy to split this into separate PRs if preferred.

## Modifications

- **Packed gate/up and Q/K/V projections** (`runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py`, `configs/models/dits/qwenimage21.py` untouched): one `MergedColumnParallelLinear` for `gate_up` feeding the bit-exact packed SiLU-mul kernel, and one for `to_qkv` viewed as strided `[B, S, H, D]` q/k/v. The fused Q/K RMSNorm+RoPE and K-RoPE+KV-pack Triton kernels (`kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/`) gain a token stride so they read those views without copies; outputs stay contiguous so attention, the prefix KV cache and BCG static buffers are unchanged. Diffusers names (`to_q/to_k/to_v`, `gate_layer/proj`) map onto shards through an instance-local `param_names_mapping` like Qwen-Image 1.0; quantized builds keep the split modules so serialized FP8/NVFP4/GGUF exports load unchanged. LoRA covers all shards.
- **SageAttention head-size fallback** (`runtime/platforms/cuda.py`, `backends/sage_attn.py`): a server-wide `sage_attn` also reaches the Qwen3-VL vision tower (head size 72), which `sageattn` asserts on, so every 2.1 edit request failed at prefill. Selection now checks the Sage backends' supported head sizes and takes the dense exact fallback the way FlashAttention already does. The Sage backend's declared head sizes are narrowed to what the package accepts.
- **Quality-gated channels_last VAE fast path** (`runtime/models/vaes/qwen_image21_vae_cuda_opt.py`, registered in `platforms/cuda.py`, gate toggled around encode in the 2.1 encoding stage): with `--quality extra-high|high`, convolutions take channels_last input with cuDNN's own padding (no `F.pad` copies, no NCHW/NHWC transposes around each conv), every `RMS_norm -> SiLU` chain runs the fused channels_last_3d Triton kernel, and the nearest-exact upsample runs the NHWC gather. Lossless default is bit-for-bit unchanged; class swaps keep every parameter under its checkpoint name.
- **Fused Wan RMSNorm+SiLU channel cap 1024 -> 2048** so the 2.1 decoder's 1152-channel levels fuse (numerics test extended with a 1152-channel case). Note: #38650 re-tiles this kernel and keeps the 1024 cap; the two will conflict textually and this one-line cap is easy to carry over.
- **Benchmark presets** `qwen21` / `qwen21-edit` in the denoise benchmark runner (skill-only, not in the nightly list).
- **Docs**: measured Cache-DiT recipes for 2.1 (defaults sit at the 0.95 SSIM threshold on generation), the VAE fast path, and the opt-in HTTP test command, which needs `SGLANG_GEN_BASELINE=1` because the harness requires a perf-baseline scenario per case id and `validate_e2e` rejects a zero baseline.

Not touched, with data: BCG never replays for a real prompt on this model (signature keys on prompt-length tensors, no 2.1 padder) but launch gaps are under 1% at 1024x1024; `torch.compile` is slower than eager; persistent KV buffers for edits and residual-gate + LayerNorm fusion are each under 1%.

## Accuracy Tests

- Unit and kernel tests on A800 and RTX 4090 (rebased tree): `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`, `test_qwen_image21.py`, `test_cuda_attention_backend.py`, `test_complex_rope.py`, `test_norm.py -k wan_rmsnorm_silu`, `test_model_fast_paths.py -k qwen21`. New cases: LoRA delta/restore on every fused shard, Diffusers-name loader round-trip into `to_qkv`/`gate_up`, quantized builds keep split modules, strided-vs-contiguous kernel equality on views produced by `project_qkv`, Sage fallback at head size 72, VAE fast path keeps names and the lossless output bit for bit.
- TP2 on two A800s with the merged weights: SSIM 0.9965 / PSNR 44.9 dB vs the pre-change TP2 image.
- Full checkpoint through the HTTP server (`test_server_qwen_image21.py`, generation and edit) passes with `SGLANG_GEN_BASELINE=1`.
- `--attention-backend sage_attn` edit now completes; the log shows the vision tower taking the dense fallback.
- Pixel checks against the pre-change lossless output, same seed, 1024x1024 / 40 steps:

| Config | A800 t2i | A800 edit | 4090 t2i | 4090 edit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| merged projections (default path) | SSIM 0.9965 / 43.3 dB | bit-identical | SSIM 0.9924 / 38.3 dB | SSIM 0.9996 / 48.6 dB |
| + VAE fast path (`--quality extra-high`) | SSIM 0.9965 / 43.3 dB | SSIM 0.9988 / 43.1 dB | SSIM 0.9924 / 38.3 dB | SSIM 0.9989 / 43.2 dB |

The merged-GEMM drift comes from cuBLAS picking different kernels for the wider N; edit stays bit-identical on A800.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Cold `sglang generate` per run, `--warmup-mode request`, medians of 5 (A800) / 5 t2i + 2 edit (4090), run-to-run spread under 0.4%. A800 resident; 4090 with the cookbook recipe (`--component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload`).

| | A800 before | A800 after | 4090 before | 4090 after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| t2i step (ms) | 318.9 | 315.3 | 427.1 | 428.6 |
| t2i prefill step 0 (ms) | 71 | 42 | 137 | 82 |
| t2i e2e (s) | 12.84 | 12.68 | 18.37 | 18.33 |
| edit step (ms) | 367.6 | 364.5 | 481.9 | 482.4 |
| edit prefill step 0 (ms) | 236 | 178 | 331 | 263 |
| edit e2e (s) | 15.37 | 15.22 | 21.25 | 21.14 |
| VAE decode stage (ms), `--quality extra-high` | 181 | 128 | 246 | 172 |
| edit encoding stage (ms), `--quality extra-high` | 259 | 240 | noisy on this host | |
| peak allocated, t2i (GB) | 34.3 | 33.3 | 18.8 | 17.8 |

The merged GEMMs give about 1% per step on A800 and are neutral on Ada steady state; prefill improves 25-40% on both. The VAE fast path cuts decode 29-30% on both GPUs. No fusion-gate fallbacks in any log.

Traces (t2i, 5 profiled steps, A800): cuBLAS GEMM 78%, FA3 15.8%, SiLU-mul 1.7%, LN-modulate 1.3%, residual gate 1.2%. VAE decode before: convs 52%, NCHW/NHWC transposes 13%, separate conv-bias adds 8%, FP32 copies for the channel RMSNorm and padding copies the rest; after: convs 67%, bias adds 10%, fused norm 5%. The remaining VAE opportunity is the conv-bias epilogue that #38650 adds for the Wan VAE.

For the record, measured lossy rows on the same setups (not enabled by default): Cache-DiT `{"residual_diff_threshold": 0.12, "max_warmup_steps": 8, "enable_taylorseer": true}` gives 2.2x (A800) / 2.0x (4090) on t2i at SSIM 0.986 / 0.985 and 2.2x / 2.1x on edit at SSIM 0.998; the defaults reach 2.7x but sit at SSIM 0.954 on t2i. SageAttention 1.x is slower than FA3 on A800.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+channels_last_3d Triton kernel; and the 2D nearest upsample runs the NHWC

+    are already laid out NHWC (size-1 dims may carry stray strides), else one
+    conversion copy at a layout boundary."""
+    n, c, h, w = x.shape
+    canonical = (h * w * c, 1, w * c, c)

+        return x
+    if x.is_contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last):
+        return x.as_strided(x.shape, canonical)
+    return x.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)

+            self.stride,
+            padding,
+            self.dilation,
+            self.groups,

+            return x
+        return nn.SiLU.forward(self, x)

+            and norm.channel_first
+            and isinstance(norm.gamma, torch.Tensor)
+            and isinstance(norm.bias, float)
+            and type(act) in (nn.SiLU, _GatedSiLU)
+            and not act.inplace

+    pairs = _norm_silu_pairs(part)

+        return None
+    for owner, norm_name, act_owner, act_name in pairs:
+        norm, act = getattr(owner, norm_name), getattr(act_owner, act_name)

+        norm._sgl_gate = gate
